Explanation of the replacement:

- We drop the old `begin: /(m|qr)?\//, end: …` rules that only handled slashes.
- We introduce a single `begin`‐only pattern (no separate `end`) with five concatenated pieces:
  1. `/(?:m|qr)?/` — optional `m` or `qr`.
  2. `/([^ \w\s\{]|\/)/` — capture the opening delimiter (any non-word, non-space, non-`{`, including `/`).
  3. `/(?:\\.|[^\\\1])*/` — match the regex body, allowing backslash-escapes or any char except backslash or the captured delimiter.
  4. `/\1/` — close on the same delimiter (back-reference to group 1).
  5. `REGEX_MODIFIERS` — allow `i`, `m`, `s`, etc. after the delimiter.
- This now correctly highlights `m(/$)/`, `m|/$|`, `m{/$}`, `m!foo!i`, `qr#bar#x`, and so on.
